question: A robo-advisor platform lets Claude generate personalized investment recommendations that are sent directly to retail customers and executed automatically, with no human financial advisor reviewing any output. Is this an appropriate use of Claude?
options: A) No, but only because automatic trade execution requires a separate brokerage license to operate
B) No, because the Usage Policy requires a qualified professional to review high-risk financial content first
C) Yes, because robo-advisory services are explicitly exempted from the Usage Policy's high-risk safeguards
D) Yes, because customers implicitly consent to automated advice by choosing a robo-advisor product
correct_answers: B) No, because the Usage Policy requires a qualified professional to review high-risk financial content first
explanations: Incorrect. A brokerage license is a separate regulatory matter and does not address the missing professional review of the AI-generated recommendations themselves.
Correct. High-risk financial recommendations require review by a qualified professional before reaching customers, and this scenario skips that review entirely, violating the safeguard.
Incorrect. Financial advice is a high-risk domain subject to the review-and-disclosure safeguards; there is no exemption for automated robo-advisory products.
Incorrect. Choosing to use a robo-advisor does not substitute for the required professional review of AI-generated financial recommendations before they take effect.
